bug_semantics: Because app/mcp/actions.ts begins with the Next.js "use server" directive, its exported async addMcpServer(clientId, config) function is remotely invocable as a Server Action. The function performs no authentication, authorization, or ENABLE_MCP check; it persists the caller-controlled ServerConfig and immediately passes its command, args, and env to initializeSingleClient. That reaches createClient in app/mcp/client.ts, where StdioClientTransport launches the supplied executable when client.connect() runs, yielding unauthenticated remote OS command execution and persistence of the malicious server configuration.
flaw_origin: Commit 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 (feat: Optimize MCP configuration logic) is the smallest causal introducer: it first added exported addMcpServer to the already server-action-marked app/mcp/actions.ts and, in the same function, copied untrusted config into mcpServers, wrote it to disk, and called initializeSingleClient(clientId, config) without any access check. The pre-existing createClient process-spawn sink then made that new one-request path exploitable. Later commit 65810d918bb599716e35c8ea515a265da909cf2f changed status/async behavior but did not originate or remove the flaw.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 shows author Kadxy <2230318258@qq.com>, committer Kadxy <2230318258@qq.com>, subject "feat: Optimize MCP configuration logic", and no message trailers; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: The official advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2jqp-6hx7-phh8 names addMcpServer in app/mcp/actions.ts, says versions through 2.16.1 are affected, lists patched versions as unknown, and says the project had not responded. The first-party report https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6757 is still open and documents a successful unauthenticated v2.16.1 Server Action POST whose attacker-controlled command/args reach StdioClientTransport and execute an OS process. In the validated clone, `git log --all -S'addMcpServer' -- app/mcp/actions.ts` finds the addition at 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4. `git blame -L 164,186 v2.16.1 -- app/mcp/actions.ts` attributes the exported function declaration and the config-write core (including `[clientId]: config` and `await updateMcpConfig(newConfig)`) to that commit; the commit's original body unconditionally calls `await initializeSingleClient(clientId, config)`. `git diff --unified=0 ce13cf61a74f7b0682c230efed2742db91c7d1b7 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 -S'addMcpServer' -- app/mcp/actions.ts` directly verifies that the immediate-parent tree has no addMcpServer and that the BIC adds the complete unchecked persistence-to-initialization path. `git cat-file -p 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4` verifies the single parent and the human-only commit object. History preserves the member commit and merges the feat-mcp branch through 4cad55379d8b32d6b46c2f6c7bd42a8f3dd17877, so this is not a squash aggregate. `git tag --contains 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4` returns v2.16.0 and v2.16.1, but not predecessor v2.15.8 (38fa3056df5fd9db915a9d4d1c5e11477de22ff6), establishing the release boundary. The current validated origin/main is defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0; its app/mcp/actions.ts still has "use server", unchecked addMcpServer at lines 164-193, and only an unused isMcpEnabled helper at lines 377-384, while app/mcp/client.ts lines 15-37 still place config.command/config.args/config.env into StdioClientTransport and connect it. No later app/mcp/actions.ts history removes or guards this path, so no upstream fix commit exists in the available history as of that main tip.
reasoning: The advisory's vulnerability is the remotely callable addMcpServer path, not merely the older existence of an MCP process-spawn sink. The sink and file-level "use server" directive predate the BIC, but the immediate parent lacks addMcpServer; 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 is the first smallest commit that joins an unauthenticated attacker-controlled Server Action input to config persistence and immediate client creation. Its original code already initialized every supplied config, so later status/async edits are neither prerequisites nor smaller introducers. Direct parent diff proves absence, preserved non-squashed ancestry proves the member commit is auditable, and tag containment places introduction after v2.15.8 and in both v2.16.0 and the reported v2.16.1. Current main retains the complete path and the public issue remains open, justifying null fix SHAs as genuinely unpatched. Finally, attribution is limited to the BIC commit object: it contains only Kadxy as human author/committer and no AI trailer or bot identity, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI despite the vulnerability remaining unpatched.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability is still unpatched in upstream history through origin/main defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0, so no fix_sha or direct_fix_sha can yet be recorded; this is an unpatched lifecycle endpoint, not an attribution evidence gap.
